fields.name: amount
fields.type: number (integer ₦ naira — rendered via formatNaira; present only on money-bearing kinds: sale, dm_received, dm_refunded, tip_received, subscription_renewal)

fields.name: creditsCount
fields.type: number (integer count — rendered via formatCredits, never as naira; present only on credits_low, trial_ending)

fields.name: actionLabel
fields.type: string (CTA button text, e.g. 'Reply now', 'Buy credits')

filtersOrSort: Mobile: client-side split into 'Now' (createdAt within last 24h of render time) vs 'Earlier' (>=24h) groups — computed with Date.now() on every render, not server-provided

Desktop (design D15): client-side regroup by consequence — 'Needs you now' (kind === 'dm_deadline'), 'Money' (amount !== undefined and not already in needs-now), 'Earlier' (everything else) — independent of the mobile time-based grouping, same underlying list
No user-facing filter/sort controls (no tabs, no type filter, no date picker) — all grouping is fixed client-side logic over the full returned list
reads.pagination: None. getNotifications() fetches the entire list in one call with no page/cursor param, no 'load more' control, no infinite scroll observed in the UI. All grouping/splitting happens client-side over the full in-memory array.

N/A — see Notification entity above. Note: the page component does NOT read res.unreadCount at all; it recomputes its own 'unread' count client-side via items.filter(n => !n.read).length. The response field is fetched but currently unused by the UI — worth flagging as a possible dead/redundant field or a future single-source-of-truth question for reconciliation.

rolesObserved: No explicit gate/role check in this screen's code (no creatorGates() call, no account-type branch). Both getNotifications() and markAllRead() call apiFetch with { authed: true } — 'any authenticated user' is the only observed requirement. The mock notification list itself mixes fan-facing kinds (credits_low, trial_ending) and creator-facing kinds (dm_deadline, sale, dm_received, kyc_verified, subscription_renewal, tip_received) in a single undifferentiated feed, implying the real backend must return a per-user feed already filtered to events relevant to that user's account type/role rather than the screen doing any client-side role filtering.

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: items === null, i.e. before getNotifications() resolves (set at the start of load() and on every re-load) — renders 5 skeleton rows
the getNotifications() promise passed to .then/.catch in the page rejects, setting error to a fixed string and rendering <ErrorState onRetry={load} />
uiStatesHandled.reachable: no — src/lib/api/notifications.ts wraps the real apiFetch call in its own try/catch and the catch branch always resolves with mockNotifications rather than rethrowing (the try-fetch-then-mock-fallback pattern). This means getNotifications() as called from the page can never actually reject in the current architecture, whether USE_MOCKS is on (apiFetch throws MockModeError immediately, caught internally) or a real backend is wired up and returns a network/server error (also caught internally and silently replaced with mock data). The page's ErrorState branch is unreachable dead code under the present data-layer design; it would only ever fire today if the mockNotifications import itself threw, which cannot happen. This is a gap the backend-wiring pass must address deliberately (e.g. rethrow on genuine network failure once mocks are removed) rather than assume the fallback pattern alone makes this state live.

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: items !== null && items.length === 0 — renders EmptyState ('Nothing to see yet') plus three CTA buttons (Browse the feed / Explore creators / Find a community)
uiStatesHandled.reachable: no — mockNotifications.items is a hardcoded 12-element array with no dev-only toggle, filter, or account-state switch that can reduce it to zero (unlike e.g. the KYC preview switcher in STUB-2). Under the current always-on mock, the notifications list can never actually be empty at runtime, so this state — though fully coded and matching design frame '2 · Empty' — cannot currently be reached by any user action.

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: items !== null && items.length > 0, on viewport < xl — renders a 'Now' section (items with createdAt within 24h) and/or an 'Earlier' section (items >= 24h), each conditionally rendered only if non-empty
uiStatesHandled.reachable: yes — with the current static mock array's relative minutesAgo() offsets, both the Now group (4 items, 2min–4h old) and the Earlier group (8 items, 24h–7d old) are always non-empty at any load time

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: items !== null && items.length > 0, on viewport >= xl — renders 'Needs you now' (kind === 'dm_deadline'), 'Money' (amount !== undefined, excluding needs-now items), and 'Earlier' (remainder), each conditionally rendered only if non-empty
uiStatesHandled.reachable: yes — with the current mock data, needsNow has 1 item, money has 5 items, and laterDesktop has 6 items, so all three sections are always populated

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: user clicks 'Mark all read' (visible only when unread > 0, computed client-side as items.filter(n => !n.read).length); on success, optimistically sets every item's read to true locally after markAllRead() resolves
uiStatesHandled.reachable: yes — the mock unread count from the seed data is 4 (4 items with read:false), so the button renders and the action is triggered by a real click; note markAllRead() itself has the exact same silent-fallback-always-succeeds issue as getNotifications() (src/lib/api/notifications.ts's catch swallows any error and returns undefined) so the action can never actually surface its own error path either — the page's catch → setError("Could not mark everything read right now.") branch is equally unreachable dead code today.

uiStatesDesigned.frame: 1 · Money and urgency first (design/screens/WAWU Notifications Search.dc.html)
uiStatesDesigned.description: Mobile populated list, time-grouped, amounts shown inline on money-bearing rows, the expiring DM row carries a 'Reply now' action button

uiStatesDesigned.frame: 1b · Earlier — approvals, billing, followers, tips (design/screens/WAWU Notifications Search.dc.html)
uiStatesDesigned.description: Mobile populated list continuation showing the 'Earlier' time group with tappable rows (chevron-right) for rejected content, subscription renewal, new follower, and a tip

uiStatesDesigned.frame: 2 · Empty — with three things to actually do (design/screens/WAWU Notifications Search.dc.html)
uiStatesDesigned.description: Mobile empty state: EmptyState('Nothing yet') plus a 'While you wait' list of three suggestion rows (Follow creators / Join a community / Notification settings) — the shipped code's empty state uses three separate CTA buttons instead of this suggestion-row layout, a layout deviation from the design source worth reconciling

uiStatesDesigned.frame: D15 · Notifications and search · money and urgency first (design/screens/desktop/WAWU Desktop Shell.dc.html)
uiStatesDesigned.description: Desktop populated list, consequence-grouped into 'Needs you now' (includes both an expiring-DM row AND a 'Your Basic renewal did not go through' subscription past-due row with a Fix button — this second needs-you-now kind has no equivalent in the 12 documented NotificationKind values or in mockNotifications.ts, a design/code gap worth flagging), 'Money' (sale/tip/payout rows), and 'Earlier' (approval/billing/follower rows)
